title: Ops guardrail activation plan & stewardship notes — Q2 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical activation plan for turning on the next set of operational guardrails tied to SLOs and service health sensors across Redwood platform services. It pairs a short rollout playbook with stewardship notes meant to live with the SRE teams after activation. Primary goal: reduce P95 latency and production error-rate variance by establishing enforcement primitives and a stewardship model so teams keep behavior under the SLOs post-launch.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: guardrail primitives (request timeout enforcement, soft rate-limits, smart retries, degraded-mode routing, basic circuit breakers), SLO signal plumbing into the observability pipeline, canary plan, and handoff to stewards.
- Out of scope: major infra refactors, long-term cost optimization recommendations, full service-level objective design for every product team (we assume SLO owners provide target numbers).

Key stakeholders:
- Project lead / owner: Priya Sharma (eng-sre)
- Activation steward: Marcus Li (platform-eng)
- Metrics & alerting SME: Lina Ortega (observability)
- Program sponsor: Sasha Nguyen, VP Eng (exec sponsor; approver for org-wide policy)
- Pilot teams: chat-service, embeddings-store, api-gateway

Success criteria (30 / 60 / 90):
- 30 days (post-canary): guardrail primitives active for pilot teams; no >3 customer-impacting rollbacks; observed reduction in p95 latency variance for pilots vs baseline by >=12%.
- 60 days: expansion to 50% of user-facing traffic; SLO dashboard shows stable error budget burn <25% for 14-day window.
- 90 days: default guardrail policy templated, adoption guidance published, stewardship rota assigned and trained.

Activation phases and high-level milestones:
1) Prep & discovery (Mar 1 - Mar 21)
   - Inventory guardrail requirements per pilot team (timeouts, retry windows, acceptable 429 behavior).
   - Map signal flow: telemetry -> metric ingestion -> SLO evaluator -> slack/pager routing.
   - Define canary success metrics and rollback thresholds.
2) Implementation & infra hooks (Mar 22 - Apr 18)
   - Implement per-service middleware for timeouts and soft rate-limits (feature flags).
   - Add SLO evaluator jobs to metrics ingestion path; validate end-to-end telemetry for pilots.
   - Create observability dashboards and burn-rate alerts for pilot teams.
3) Canary activation (Apr 19 - May 2)
   - Enable guardrails behind feature flags for pilot traffic slice (5% -> 20% -> 50%).
   - Daily rollout standups, fast rollback path defined, runbook in Slack pinned.
4) Expansion & templating (May 3 - May 31)
   - Iterate policy templates for timeouts/rate-limits per workload class.
   - Publish docs + short how-to for teams to opt into the guardrails.
5) Stewardship & handoff (Jun 1 - Jun 14)
   - Assign stewards per service and create a 12-week monitoring checklist.
   - Run a 2-hour stewardship workshop and capture common runbook items.

Tactical checklist (short):
- [ ] Inventory for pilot teams completed (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Feature flags wired and tested in staging (owner: platform-eng)
- [ ] SLO evaluator job validated for 7-day backfill (owner: observability)
- [ ] Canary rollback automation tested (owner: release-engineering)
- [ ] Runbook drafted and linked in each service repo (owner: service owners)
- [ ] Stewardship rota published and pager rules verified (owner: SRE lead)

Canary runbook (short):
- Target windows: 8 AM - 5 PM PST weekdays for first two canary days.
- Rollout pauses at 5% and 20% for 2 x 30-minute observation windows.
- Automated rollback triggers: sustained 2x baseline error-rate for 10 minutes OR SLO burn-rate > 5x for 5 minutes.
- Manual rollback criteria: product owner flags customer-impacting behavior.

Observability & alerting notes:
- Ensure the SLO evaluator exposes both short-window and long-window burn rates (1m, 5m, 1h, 24h).
- Add a neutral-level Slack channel alert for early warning and reserved PagerDuty escalation for confirmed degradation.
- Tag telemetry from canary slice with guardrail-feature flag id so we can slice metrics easily.

Stewardship model (how to keep it alive):
- Each service must nominate a Steward (rotation 6 weeks). Steward responsibilities: run weekly SLO digest, escalate regressions, own minor policy parameter tuning, and sign off quarterly on guardrail relevance.
- Platform SRE team will own guardrail template maintenance, major policy changes, and cross-team coordination.
- Add a short checklist to new-hire SRE onboarding: how to interpret burn-rate signals and where to look for canary metadata.

Open questions / hazards (notes to self):
- How do we handle services with very bursty traffic patterns where soft rate-limits generate unacceptable tail behavior? Need hybrid policy or per-endpoint exceptions.
- Bandwidth on product teams to implement client-side retry/backoff best-practices — may need solutions engineering runbook.
- Cost impact of extra metric cardinality; observability lead must sign off on retention vs cardinality tradeoffs.
- Legal/Compliance: confirm that any request-level sampling used for telemetry respects PII redaction policy.

Communications & governance:
- Weekly activation standup M/W/F 30m during canary weeks; owners must post short notes to the activation thread in #sre-ops.
- Steering sync biweekly with program sponsor for risk sign-off and any org-wide policy exceptions.

Quick meetings & checkpoints (calendar skeleton):
- Mar 5: Kickoff, alignment on success metrics (attendees: stakeholders)
- Mar 18: Pilot inventory review (task owners present)
- Apr 12: Feature flag readiness review
- Apr 19: Canary day zero preflight
- May 10: Expansion readiness checkpoint
- Jun 8: Stewardship workshop

Post-activation artifacts to create (deliverables):
- Guardrail policy templates in the platform repo (PR example: linked above).
- SLO dashboard template per workload class and a short cookbook.
- Stewardship checklist and rotation calendar (Google Sheet).
- Short retrospective doc at 30-day and 90-day marks (lessons learned).

Short retrospective notes (preliminary, to fill during rollout):
- What unexpected client-side behaviors surfaced during canary?
- Which guardrail parameters required frequent tuning?
- Where did our observability signal fall short?

Rough risk & mitigation table (one-liners):
- Risk: false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds + gradual canary slice.
- Risk: pilot teams lack bandwidth. Mitigation: solutions engineering pairing and small acceptance criteria.
- Risk: alert fatigue from extra signals. Mitigation: tiered alerts and short window noise filters.

Immediate next steps (today / this week):
- Priya: finalize pilot inventory and publish to the shared activation spreadsheet.
- Marcus: create the platform feature-flag branch and wire basic timeouts middleware in staging.
- Lina: provision SLO evaluator job with 7-day backfill for pilot metrics and create initial dashboards.
- Ethan: draft the canary slack template and rollback command snippets for release-engineering to wire.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a small 'policy observability' metric that measures how often guardrail parameters are changed — trend it.
- Could use a quarterly "guardrail review" light retro during team health check-ins.
- Keep the first rollout conservative. We can loosen later once stewards are comfortable.

Attachments / refs: link the PR, the JIRA epic, and the confluence guide above.

-- end of activation brief --

(Informal, iterate freely here. This is a working doc; move to Confluence once we have a stable playbook.)
